name: Apache Kafka
summary: A distributed event-streaming platform that stores partitioned event logs durably, decouples producers from consumers, and supports replayable stream processing.

features.name: Partitioned append-only event storage
features.description: Kafka organizes events into topics, distributes each topic across partitions on brokers, and appends each published event to a partition. Consumers of one topic-partition observe events in the order written to that partition.
benefits: Provides a scalable unit for parallel reads and writes
Preserves per-partition ordering for keyed event streams
Supports sequential durable storage and repeated reads
costs: Ordering is scoped to a partition rather than a whole topic or cluster
Partition-key selection affects locality and load balance
Partition count and placement become long-lived operational decisions

features.name: Retained and replayable event history
features.description: Kafka does not delete events merely because a consumer has read them. Topic retention determines when older events are discarded, allowing events to be read repeatedly and processed retrospectively.
benefits: Decouples event production from consumer timing
Supports backfills, replay, and multiple independent consumers
Turns the messaging substrate into a durable event history
costs: Storage cost grows with the configured retention window and event volume
Consumers must manage their position and replay semantics
Retention is not the same as permanent archival

features.name: Producer and consumer decoupling
features.description: Kafka's official introduction describes producers and consumers as fully decoupled and agnostic of each other. Producers publish events while consumers independently subscribe to and process them.
benefits: Allows independent scaling and deployment of producers and consumers
Supports multiple consumers with different processing purposes
Provides a stable integration boundary between services
costs: Schemas, compatibility, and event ownership must be governed across teams
End-to-end behavior becomes asynchronous and harder to reason about locally
Consumer lag and replay can create operational backlogs

features.name: Replicated topic partitions
features.description: Kafka can replicate topic-partitions across brokers and even across regions or datacenters so that multiple brokers retain copies for fault tolerance and availability.
benefits: Maintains copies of event data across broker failures
Supports maintenance and failure recovery without a single storage copy
Applies the replication unit to the same partition unit used for scaling
costs: Replication consumes additional storage and network bandwidth
Availability and durability depend on replica placement and cluster state
Failure handling adds coordination to the append path

features.name: Composable stream-processing pipeline
features.description: Kafka provides APIs for processing event streams, including transformations, stateful aggregations, joins, and windowing, with input topics transformed into output topics.
benefits: Expresses event-processing stages as connected stream transformations
Supports both real-time and retrospective processing over retained events
Allows derived streams to be consumed by further applications
costs: Stateful processing requires checkpointing and recovery design
Topology behavior depends on partitioning and event-time assumptions
A pipeline introduces cumulative latency and operational coupling

mathematical_views.question: How do topic events map to ordered partition sequences while enabling parallel distribution?
assumptions: Each partition is modeled as an append-only sequence with a local order
A key-to-partition mapping is stable enough for the required ordering scope
The model does not infer a total order across partitions

mathematical_views.question: How can the same retained event sequence drive multiple consumers or be replayed to reconstruct derived state?
assumptions: Consumers maintain a position in the retained sequence
Event processing is deterministic or explicitly models external effects
Retention has not removed the required prefix of the event history

mathematical_views.question: Which observable event-history properties are preserved when a partition is represented by multiple broker replicas?
assumptions: Replica coordination provides the availability and durability behavior claimed by the deployment
The comparison concerns observable retained events and ordering, not identical internal timing
Failure and recovery transitions are included in the refinement model

benefits: Parallel scale with local ordering and sequential append behavior
costs: Cross-partition ordering and load balance require explicit design

benefits: Consumer independence, replay, and retrospective processing
costs: Retention storage, lag management, and schema evolution obligations

benefits: Independent service evolution and fan-out
costs: Asynchronous failure modes and distributed contract governance

benefits: Fault tolerance and high availability for retained event data
costs: Additional storage, network traffic, and coordination

benefits: Reusable transformations from input topics to derived topics
costs: State recovery, topology management, and cumulative latency
